data.narrative:
Planet Labs is a publicly traded Space & Aerospace company founded by Boshuizen, Marshall, and Schingler. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 3 same-sector, same-stage peers: Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B), and Astroscale ($840M).

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Across these 3 public Space & Aerospace comparables, the median valuation stands at $2.9B, with a range spanning $840M to $40.0B. A revenue-based P/S approach cannot be applied, as the target's revenue figure is unavailable in the dataset. The wide dispersion among peers—driven primarily by Rocket Lab's significantly higher valuation—introduces material uncertainty into any single-point estimate.

The analysis supports a triangulated valuation range of $2.5B to $3.3B, centered on a median of $2.9B. This range reflects the peer-median method as the sole quantitatively grounded approach. The current market valuation of $7.56B substantially exceeds this implied range, suggesting either market-embedded growth expectations not captured in current peer multiples, or valuation dispersion typical of early-stage aerospace. Key uncertainties include the relevance of the three-peer sample given the sector's heterogeneity, and the absence of revenue visibility to apply sector P/S benchmarks.
